title: Combined Phacoemulsification and 360-Degree Suture Trabeculotomy Ab Externo in Primary Chronic Angle Closure Glaucoma: A Modified Technique

indication: primary chronic angle-closure glaucoma with cataract; no previous intraocular surgery (retrospective, single surgeon, one eye per patient, all patients completed at least 12 months of follow-up)

notes: Role: the modified technique is the variant the article was written to assess (title and Purpose), so it is the treated arm; the standard ab externo technique is the control.

Context: 360-degree suture trabeculotomy combined with phacoemulsification is recorded as angle_mims (protocol: trabeculotomy and other angle procedures combined with cataract surgery). Both arms also include a trabeculo-Descemet window and subconjunctival 5-fluorouracil.
Method: the article does not name a tonometer.

Reference kind: patients were on topical antiglaucoma medications before surgery (Table 2 R3 and Table 4 R2) and no washout is described; the medication status at the preoperative measurement is not stated explicitly.

Postoperative re-interventions (ab interno revision, diode cyclophotocoagulation, Ahmed valve) occurred in a few eyes; the article does not state that these eyes were removed from the visit means, so no outcome-defined exclusion applies.
Mean number of antiglaucoma medications per visit is tabulated in Table 4 (not extracted).
